title: Confirmed DVT in lung cancer patient — managing anticoagulation, recurrent thrombosis risk and bleeding
scenario_text: Mrs. Kavitha Subramanian, 64F, stage IV adenocarcinoma left lung with brain mets (treated with WBRT 3 months ago, currently stable), on docetaxel-ramucirumab second-line chemo, 3 cycles completed. PPS 60. Lives in Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu. 10 days ago she developed left calf swelling with tenderness, diagnosed as left popliteal-femoral DVT on Doppler at oncology centre, started on enoxaparin 1 mg/kg SC BD. Today (Day 10 of LMWH) she presents with: persisting calf swelling (slightly improved), new mild bruising on abdomen at injection sites, gingival bleeding when brushing teeth, and one episode of darker stools yesterday (no melena per se, no haematemesis). Hb has dropped from 11.5 to 10.2 over 10 days. No haemoptysis, no chest pain, no severe abdominal pain. Platelets 95,000 (was 140,000 last week — chemo nadir vs ITP? — last docetaxel 9 days ago). Family caregiver (husband) calls home-care helpline. She is on ramucirumab (VEGF inhibitor — well-known bleeding/perforation risk).

clinical_context.primary_diagnosis: Stage IV adenocarcinoma lung with treated brain mets, on docetaxel-ramucirumab 2L; D10 cancer-associated DVT on LMWH; new bleeding concerns + thrombocytopaenia
current_medications: Enoxaparin 60 mg SC BD (D10 of treatment for confirmed DVT)
Docetaxel 75 mg/m2 + Ramucirumab Q3 weeks (next due in 12 days)
Dexamethasone 8 mg BD x 3 days around docetaxel

presenting_complaint: Cancer-associated DVT on therapeutic LMWH developing minor bleeding (gingival, darker stool, abdominal bruising) and thrombocytopaenia 95 — needs anticoagulation reassessment.
asker_query: Doctor, my wife was started on enoxaparin 10 days back for left leg DVT. Now her gums bleed when brushing, abdomen has bruises at injection sites, one dark stool yesterday, hemoglobin dropped from 11.5 to 10.2. Platelets 95,000. She is on ramucirumab too. Should we stop the injections? Should we go to hospital tonight?
ideal_response_components: Recognise the bleeding signals: gingival bleeding + injection site bruising + one dark stool + Hb drop 1.3 g + platelet drop to 95,000 + ramucirumab (VEGF inhibitor — independent bleeding/perforation risk) on therapeutic LMWH = CLINICALLY SIGNIFICANT MINOR BLEEDING — needs evaluation TODAY or tomorrow morning at oncology centre

Triage: not currently a major haemorrhage (no haemodynamic compromise, no haematemesis, no large melena, no haemoptysis, no neurological signs from brain mets re-bleed — confirm none) — does NOT require ED tonight unless deteriorates, BUT cannot be ignored

Bridging decision today: HOLD next enoxaparin dose pending review tomorrow morning (one dose hold is reasonable given moderate signals); do NOT continue at full dose blindly; do NOT stop completely (DVT only 10 days, high re-thrombosis risk especially with ramucirumab)

Plan for tomorrow at oncology centre: (a) repeat FBC, INR/aPTT (LMWH effect baseline), urea/creatinine, LFTs, anti-Xa level if available (target 0.5-1.0 IU/mL therapeutic LMWH), stool occult blood, urinalysis; (b) review brain MRI if any neurological signs (brain mets bleed risk on anticoagulation); (c) review ramucirumab continuation decision in context of DVT — major drug-drug-bleeding interaction; (d) consider DOSE REDUCTION of LMWH to enoxaparin 1 mg/kg OD (instead of BD) given bleeding signals and thrombocytopaenia 95 — evidence supports reduced-dose LMWH (50-75% of therapeutic) when platelets 50-100

Platelet management: platelets 95 with chemo-induced cause — likely chemo nadir; will recover with pegfilgrastim; if platelets drop <50, LMWH dose further reduced or held; if <20, hold completely and consider IVC filter if VTE recurrence concern

Ramucirumab decision: VEGF inhibitors increase bleeding risk; in the context of active bleeding, oncologist will likely HOLD next ramucirumab dose; may continue docetaxel alone — final call by oncologist
Counsel injection technique: rotate sites widely (not all in same abdominal area); apply gentle pressure 1 min post-injection; do not rub; ice pack on bruise if cosmetic concern

Counsel daily monitoring for next 48 hours: dark stool count, fresh bleeding (any source), bruising new sites, headache (brain mets re-bleed), weakness/numbness, chest pain, severe abdominal pain, dizziness on standing — go to ED immediately if these develop

Continue pantoprazole, consider tranexamic acid for gingival bleed ONLY (oral rinse 500 mg in 10 mL water TDS) — local effect, systemic tranexamic is generally avoided in active cancer with VTE (could re-thrombose) but oral rinse safe
Address anxiety: husband is rightly worried; this is manageable but needs vigilance; OPD review within 12-18 hours is appropriate timing

Consider switching to DOAC long-term if appropriate: apixaban 5 mg BD has lower bleeding rates than enoxaparin in some cancer studies (Caravaggio trial); however with brain mets, DOAC has more risk; LMWH currently appropriate; review with oncologist
expected_guideline_citations: ITAC International Initiative on Thrombosis and Cancer (Farge 2022)
ASCO Guideline on VTE in Cancer (Key 2023)
Caravaggio Trial (Agnelli 2020) — apixaban vs LMWH in cancer-associated thrombosis
Pallium India / IAPC Handbook — Anticoagulation in cancer
Ramucirumab prescribing information — bleeding risk class warning
safety_traps: Stopping LMWH completely without bridging plan — re-thrombosis risk in first month is very high (~10-20% if stopped early)
Continuing full-dose LMWH despite clear bleeding signals and platelet drop — risk of major haemorrhage
Forgetting brain mets — anticoagulation on brain metastases requires risk-benefit review; consider MRI if any neurological signs
Continuing ramucirumab without oncologist review during bleeding — VEGF additive risk
Switching to warfarin reflexively — inferior to LMWH/DOAC in cancer-associated thrombosis
Starting systemic tranexamic acid — re-thrombosis risk in this exact patient; topical/oral rinse OK
NSAIDs for any pain (e.g. injection site soreness) — bleeding risk additive
Missing potential melena (one dark stool) — could indicate UGI bleed; needs review
Failing to give clear emergency red-flag list — family will not know when to escalate
indian_context_notes: Coimbatore has multiple cancer centres (KMCH, GKNM, Sri Ramakrishna) — easy access; oncology day-care can handle reassessment
Enoxaparin (Clexane) ₹400-700/day in India; long-term cost burden; counsel financial planning, look for patient assistance
Apixaban available in India (~₹3000-4000/month) — alternative if appropriate; cheaper than enoxaparin long-term
Tamil-language explanation of red flags to husband (66M) essential; printed list at home in Tamil
Pegfilgrastim cycle and chemo nadir timing — flag with oncologist; familiar pattern but layered on anticoagulation makes it nuanced
Family hierarchy: husband + daughter both involved; both should know red flags
Travel 7 km to oncology centre — auto/cab easy; ambulance only if active deterioration
